topics.flagship-ru-ua: Russia's FSB says it arrested two men who were preparing a Ukrainian FPV drone attack on Moscow's air defenses and a power facility. Separately, Russia said on Oct. 26 that it will not slow its offensive despite upcoming U.S.-brokered talks, though it could accept local "humanitarian" ceasefires. Zelenskyy reportedly says Ukraine has waited almost a month for Hegseth to approve Patriot missiles. Russian strikes continue to kill civilians across several oblasts, and Ukraine reportedly hit a missile parts plant in Oryol. European defence ministers are meeting in Paris on Ukraine support, and a Musk-Ukraine dispute over Starlink use for drone strikes continues.
topics.flagship-ir-il: Israeli forces killed at least five people in Gaza, including a 7-year-old girl, and the reported toll has reached 74,555, including 1,559 killed since last year's ceasefire. Egypt's parliament authorised military aid for Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks on the kingdom, though Cairo has ruled out strikes on Yemen. On Iran, US forces are reportedly ready to strike within 96 hours if Trump orders it, and Trump says he will soon decide whether to "make a deal" or "finish it off". Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani delegations are in Tehran seeking to prevent renewed fighting. Netanyahu, on the eve of Israel's election, suggested he and Trump could restart the war on Iran, while the IDF chief reportedly resists a pre-election operation.
topics.T15: Cyclone preparations are underway in India. Vijayawada has opened 24/7 control rooms, and Odisha is mobilising personnel and cancelling officials' leave as a severe cyclonic storm nears the Andhra coast. In the US, the Four Corners region faces major flooding with evacuations still in place, and record high tides are flooding coastal streets. Other items are minor or forward-looking, including a Super El Niño outlook for Malaysia and a tsunami evacuation planning tool.
topics.T01: Algeria will reportedly send troops to Niger to protect energy facilities near the Libyan border, its first foreign deployment since 1973. Fox News, as relayed by Sputnik, reports the Pentagon is preparing US military bases to operate autonomously for at least 90 days in a possible conflict. The remaining items are opinion or analysis pieces on Russia's threat to America and on how a Democratic win in November might affect US foreign policy.
topics.T02: The UN Security Council held a briefing on children and armed conflict as a signature event of Greece's October presidency, marking 30 years since the General Assembly created the mandate. Human Rights Watch says the Houthis used explosives on Oct. 18 to damage a key road into besieged Taizz, Yemen. Western governments issued a statement marking one year since the El Fasher atrocity in Sudan. UN figures cited show conflict-related sexual violence cases nearly quadrupled between 2022 and 2025. Other items cover Gaza schooling, Myanmar and Afghanistan accountability efforts, and a water project in Nigeria.
topics.T03: An Illinois man, Matthew Ungelsbee, 37, is charged with mailing threatening letters containing white powder to members of Congress, one with a note reading "HAH enjoy the gift." The story was widely carried, with eight outlets. The only other item is a research report on a coating under development at Northwestern University that could neutralize nerve agents.
topics.T04: A Swiss woman treated for Ebola in Nigeria has been medically evacuated to Switzerland with her husband. Uganda has imposed a 21-day quarantine on citizens returning from DR Congo and will bar most travellers who have been in DR Congo from transiting. Kenya released 20 contacts of its first imported Ebola case after they completed 21 days of monitoring without symptoms. Other items are research or commentary, plus an unconfirmed report that bird flu is spreading on a mink farm.
topics.T05: Lula won a fourth term in Brazil after overturning a first-round deficit, and one outlet reports the right-wing side concluded the election was rigged. Serbian voters ended Vučić's 12-year dominance in a record turnout. In Libya, Saddam Haftar is reportedly positioning himself for the presidency as the US seeks a unity deal. Other items include a US Justice Department lawsuit over Alaska's Senate election certification and Maria Corina Machado's return to Caracas.
topics.T06: France saw another weekend of mass protests, with Interior Ministry figures of over 410,000 participants nationwide (about 110,000 in Paris) and nearly 1,000 detentions. Authorities deployed about 70,000 security personnel, and the demonstrations were largely peaceful. The government and its critics dispute whether to call the unrest riots or protests, and a Steelers-Saints NFL game in Paris went ahead despite the unrest. Air Canada crews in some European cities were rerouted. A single outlet reports about 30 dead in Sri Lankan prison riots.
topics.T07: Only one source: retired Gen. Jack Keane told Fox News that Iran is rebuilding nuclear sites despite ongoing peace talks with the US. This is an unverified claim from one commentator.
topics.T08: Jordan said it struck "terrorist organizations" in Syria on Monday in retaliation for the Oct. 23 attack on a church in Karak during a funeral service, which killed eight and wounded 40. The story was carried by seven outlets, and the King vowed the "harshest retaliation." The public security chief said the three attackers did not plan the attack in advance. Other items include allegations of Ukrainian support for Tuareg rebels in Mali and a Russia-Africa summit in Moscow.
topics.T10: Items are mixed and mostly low-signal. Hegseth's new autonomous command (AUTOWARCOM) faces funding doubts because it depends on a reconciliation bill whose passage is uncertain. The US Air Force secretary disclosed that the Space Force has on-orbit space control weapons. Germany's Merz is touring Asia on security and supply-chain concerns, and Korean shipbuilders are weighing the costs of localisation demands in Western naval rearmament. A US littoral combat ship made a routine port call in Colombo.
topics.T11: Israel is holding its largest drill in years, mobilising multiple divisions to counter border infiltration, and one analyst invokes the 1973 war. Japan's Type-25 antiship missile system went mobile during a large joint exercise, with a reported range of about 620 miles. The Indian Navy's INS Trishul conducted a PASSEX with an Italian warship, and India and Australia are holding AUSTRAHIND 2026.
topics.T12: Japanese companies, including GMO Internet, are compensating users after waves of cyberattacks disrupted internet services and raised concerns about economic stability. The story was carried by three outlets. A separate item covers a startup raising $15 million to counter AI-enabled fraud and hacking.
topics.T13: Coverage is sparse and largely opinion. One outlet reports over 30,000 people marched in Madrid over the ongoing mass migrant arrivals in Ceuta, nearing its third month. Other items are commentary on migration in Ireland and Assam, an asylum ruling, and a UNHCR goodwill ambassador appointment.
topics.T14: The US State Department ordered non-emergency staff and family members to leave Saudi Arabia on Oct. 21, affecting the Riyadh embassy and the Jeddah consulate, amid rising threats after deadly strikes. CNN reportedly says the US is likely to downsize more diplomatic missions in the Middle East in the coming days. Both reports come from single outlets.

bluf: Israeli forces killed at least five people in Gaza, including a 7-year-old girl, and the reported toll has reached 74,555, including 1,559 killed since last year's ceasefire. A Swiss woman treated for Ebola in Nigeria has been medically evacuated to Switzerland with her husband, and Uganda has imposed a 21-day quarantine on returnees from DR Congo, while Kenya released 20 contacts of its first imported case after 21 days without symptoms. The UN Security Council held a briefing on children and armed conflict under Greece's October presidency, marking 30 years of the mandate. Russia's FSB says it arrested two men preparing a Ukrainian FPV drone attack on Moscow's air defenses and a power facility. Moscow also said it will not slow its offensive ahead of U.S.-brokered talks but could accept local humanitarian ceasefires. Egypt's parliament authorised military aid for Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks, though Cairo has ruled out strikes on Yemen. Separately, US forces in the Middle East are reportedly ready to strike Iran within 96 hours if ordered, and Trump says he will soon choose between a deal and renewed military action. The State Department has ordered non-emergency staff to leave Saudi Arabia, and CNN reportedly says more Middle East diplomatic drawdowns are likely in the coming days.
